question: Will the Argentine Senate give final approval to the 'Ley Hojarasca' before August 8, 2026?

factors.description: Most recent reporting (El Litoral) says Ley Hojarasca has been displaced to August 13, outside the July 25-Aug 7 resolution window
August 6 session is confirmed but dedicated to resuming the contentious property rights bill (cuarto intermedio), expected to consume the session under the one-main-topic-per-session norm
Property rights bill has failed/postponed 5 times on quorum/votes; if it collapses quickly on Aug 6 the session may simply end rather than pivoting to Hojarasca
Hojarasca has a favorable committee dictamen and clear majority; if reached on the floor it passes easily and uncontentiously
Infobae still listed both bills for Aug 6 and block leaders agreed to include Hojarasca on the agenda; genuine schedule fluidity leaves residual chance it is reached in-window

summary: The Ley Hojarasca will very likely become law eventually — it has a favorable Senate committee dictamen and a clear governing majority (LLA+PRO+UCR+provincial allies), and passes easily if it reaches the floor. But this question hinges narrowly on whether the definitive Senate floor vote occurs between July 25 and Aug 7. The only plausible in-window session is Aug 6, which is confirmed but dedicated to resuming the contentious property-rights bill (its 5th postponement). The most recent reporting (El Litoral) says Hojarasca has been displaced to Aug 13 — outside the window. The binding constraint is floor time, not votes. Residual YES probability (~15%) comes from genuine schedule ambiguity (Infobae still listed both bills for Aug 6, block leaders had agreed to include it) and the chance the property bill collapses quickly enough that the majority pivots to dispatch the uncontentious Hojarasca while quorum holds.
reasoning:
**Forecast: 14% (NO likely)**

The Ley Hojarasca is essentially certain to become law eventually — it has a favorable Senate dictamen and a clear governing majority, and passes easily whenever it reaches the floor. But this question is narrowly about timing: whether the definitive floor vote lands between July 25 and August 7, 2026.

Key findings:
- The only plausible in-window session is **August 6**, which is confirmed but dedicated to resuming the contentious **property-rights bill** (its 5th postponement), expected to consume the session.
- The most recent reporting (El Litoral) says Hojarasca has been **displaced to August 13** — outside the resolution window.
- The binding constraint is floor time, not votes.

Residual YES probability comes from schedule fluidity (Infobae still listed both bills for Aug 6; block leaders had agreed to include it) and the chance the property bill collapses fast enough for the majority to dispatch the uncontentious Hojarasca while quorum holds.
